title: The diagonal is a regular immersion
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth,
separated, of pure
relative dimension $d$, and put $W=X\times_YX$ with projections
$p_1,p_2$ and diagonal $\Delta:X\hookrightarrow W$. Then $\Delta$
is a regular closed immersion of
pure codimension $d$, and its normal bundle is canonically

$$
N_{\Delta/W}\;\cong\;T_{X/Y}
$$

(the relative tangent bundle of $f$).

proof.text: Work in the chapter's separated finite-type setting over a field, with d ≥ 1 as required by [def-pur-regular-immersion]. Since f is separated, its diagonal Δ is a closed immersion. Near each point z of X, Mathlib SmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_isStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension supplies affine opens V ⊂ X and U ⊂ Y, with z ∈ V and f(V) ⊂ U, on which the ring map R = Γ(U) → A = Γ(V) is standard smooth of relative dimension d. Mathlib RingHom.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_etale_mvPolynomial then gives an etale R-algebra map ψ:R[X_0,…,X_{d-1}] → A. The diagonal of V → U is, under the affine-spectrum identifications and diagonal_SpecMap, induced by multiplication μ:A ⊗_R A → A.

Put r_i = 1 ⊗ ψ(X_i) − ψ(X_i) ⊗ 1. These d elements belong to ker μ, and μ is surjective since μ(a ⊗ 1) = a. The etale map ψ is flat by Mathlib RingHom.Etale.iff_flat_and_formallyUnramified, so [lem-sc-flat-polynomial-diagonal-differences-weakly-regular] makes the list (r_0,…,r_{d-1}) weakly regular in A ⊗_R A. By [lem-sc-etale-polynomial-diagonal-kernel-clearance], there is e ∈ A ⊗_R A with μ(e) = 1 and e·ker μ ⊂ (r_0,…,r_{d-1}). Thus [lem-sc-affine-regular-immersion-kernel-criterion] applies to μ and proves affine-local regularity of this diagonal with d weakly regular generators.

The square formed by V → X and the diagonals of V → U and X → Y is cartesian, and V ×_U V → W is an open immersion. Hence the affine-local weakly regular generators just obtained give such generators near Δ(z). Away from the image of Δ its ideal is the unit ideal; since d > 0, a list of d copies of 1 is weakly regular and generates that ideal. This is the construction of AlgebraicGeometry.isRegularImmersion_diagonal: every point of W has an affine neighbourhood on which the diagonal ideal is generated by a weakly regular list of length d.

The product W is locally of finite type over the field, hence locally Noetherian by Mathlib LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian. At each z ∈ X take an affine neighbourhood U of Δ(z) and a weakly regular list r of length d generating the diagonal ideal. The stalk O_{W,Δ(z)} is a flat localization of Γ(W,U), by Mathlib IsLocalization.flat, so the list of germs remains weakly regular by RingTheory.Sequence.IsWeaklyRegular.of_flat. Since Δ(z) belongs to the zero locus of the diagonal ideal, each generator germ is a nonunit in this local ring. Mathlib IsLocalRing.isRegular_iff_isWeaklyRegular_of_subset_maximalIdeal makes the list regular. The closed-immersion identity Scheme.Hom.ker_stalkMap, together with Ideal.map_ofList, identifies its generated ideal with the kernel of the stalk map O_{W,Δ(z)} → O_{X,z}.

Apply Mathlib ringKrullDim_add_length_eq_ringKrullDim_of_isRegular to this regular sequence in the Noetherian local stalk. The stalk map of a closed immersion is surjective; RingHom.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective identifies the quotient by its kernel with O_{X,z}, and ringKrullDim_eq_of_ringEquiv transports its dimension. This gives exactly dim O_{W,Δ(z)} = dim O_{X,z} + d. Index the regular list by Fin d using List.get and List.ofFn_get; its range is precisely its list membership set, so its span is the required kernel ideal. These two stalk clauses, together with d ≥ 1 and the closed-immersion property, prove that Δ is a regular closed immersion of pure codimension d in the sense of [def-pur-regular-immersion].

blueprint_update.statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth,
separated, of pure
relative dimension $d$, and put $W=X\times_YX$ with projections
$p_1,p_2$ and diagonal $\Delta:X\hookrightarrow W$. Then $\Delta$
is a regular closed immersion of
pure codimension $d$.

proof.text:
By [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form], $f$ is etale locally the
projection $\mathbf A^d_Y\to Y$; on the model, $\Delta$ is the zero
section of $\mathbf A^d$, a regular closed immersion of codimension
$d$ with normal bundle the trivial rank-$d$ bundle, which under the
identification is $T_{X/Y}$. Regular immersions, their codimension
and their normal bundles are etale local (and compatible with etale
base change), hence the assertion.
